# -C names the directory every filesystem path resolves against.
# It does not change the process working directory, so a path that is
# already absolute keeps working and the tree outside it is untouched.

# Relative source, output and resource paths all resolve against -C.
md2html -C site -html out -html-ext html -css theme.css -data-json data.json -templates tmpl docs
exists site/out/index.html
grep 'background: #eee' site/out/guide.html
grep 'data: Widgets' site/out/guide.html
! exists out

# The same run named from inside the directory produces the same page.
cd site
md2html -html out2 -html-ext html -css theme.css -data-json data.json -templates tmpl docs
cmp out/guide.html out2/guide.html
cd ..

# An absolute source still renders under -C, which is only a base.
md2html -C site $WORK/site/docs/guide.md
stdout 'Guide'

# A default (empty) source is rooted at -C, and so is stdin: neither
# names a directory of its own.
md2html -C site -html out3 -html-ext html
exists site/out3/docs/guide.html

md2html -C site -http :9061 - &
wait-port :9061
curl -s http://localhost:9061/docs/guide
stdout 'Guide'

# A -C that is not a directory is reported, even with nothing relative
# left to resolve.
! md2html -C site/theme.css $WORK/site/docs/guide.md
stderr 'chdir'
! md2html -C site/nowhere $WORK/site/docs/guide.md
stderr 'chdir'

-- site/docs/guide.md --
# Guide

A page about widgets.

-- site/tmpl/layout.html --
{{define "layout"}}<!doctype html>
<title>{{.Title}}</title>
<style>{{.CustomCSS}}</style>
<p>{{with .Data}}data: {{.product}}{{end}}</p>
{{.Content}}
{{end}}

-- site/theme.css --
body { background: #eee; }

-- site/data.json --
{"product": "Widgets"}
